title: Money: Segments
description: The descriptive half of the money picture: not how much, but how many, and of what. Refund and dispute counts split by plan, card, region, reason and customer tenure, and the subscription churn behind them. Sums here are COUNTS first; for authoritative money totals use the Money Out dashboard, which reads the same deduplicated ledger without the tag splits. Every split is a bounded label or an ISO country code: no names, no emails, no addresses, no card numbers. Values read 'unknown' where the segment was never resolved, which is not the same as zero, and history imported by a backfill is deliberately unsegmented. Concessions (credit notes, coupons, credit grants, balance credits) are recorded in the ledger but not segmented: they attach to a customer rather than to a charge, so there is no card and no charge age to read. They will always show as 'unknown' here, and belong on the Money Out dashboard instead.

panels.title: Refunds
panels.description: How MANY refunds were issued in this window, from the same deduplicated ledger the Money Out dashboard sums. One point per refund, whoever issued it, including refunds made straight from the Stripe Dashboard.

panels.title: Refunded
panels.description: What those refunds cost, net of refunds that later failed.

panels.title: Partial refunds
panels.description: Refunds for less than the remaining charge. A rising share usually means goodwill gestures rather than cancellations.

panels.title: Same-day refunds
panels.description: Refunded within a day of paying. Buyer's remorse and mis-clicks, which is a checkout problem rather than a product one.

panels.title: Fees lost to refunds
panels.description: Stripe keeps the original processing fee when you refund, so every refund costs a little more than the amount handed back. This is that residue.

panels.title: Refunds with no plan resolved
panels.description: Refunds whose plan could not be worked out: enrichment switched off in /config, the per-sweep lookup budget exhausted, a one-off charge with no subscription behind it, or a row imported by a history backfill (which never resolves segments). A large number here means every split on this dashboard is reading a partial picture.

panels.title: Refunds by plan

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "money_out")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and r.category == "refund")
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "plan_tier"])
  |> group(columns: ["plan_tier"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)

panels.description: Which plan we refund most, by COUNT. Read it next to the amount chart beside it: the plan with the most refunds and the plan with the most refunded money are often not the same, and they are different problems.

panels.title: Refunded amount by plan

panels.description: The same refunds weighted by money. 'custom' means a non-canonical price, 'unknown' means the plan was never resolved.

panels.title: Disputes opened
panels.description: Chargebacks where the money was actually withdrawn, counted from the ledger.

panels.title: Disputed
panels.description: Money withdrawn by chargeback, net of reinstatements.

panels.title: Win rate

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dispute_outcomes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and (r.outcome == "won" or r.outcome == "lost"))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "outcome"])
  |> group()
  |> reduce(
      identity: {wanted: 0.0, total: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        wanted: accumulator.wanted + (if r.outcome == "won" then r._value else 0.0),
        total: accumulator.total + r._value
      })
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _value: if r.total > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.wanted / r.total else 0.0 }))

panels.description: Won as a share of disputes that reached a verdict. Inquiries closed by refunding (outcome 'prevented') are excluded on purpose: they never went to a verdict, and counting them as wins would flatter the number.

panels.title: Disputes on prepaid or debit
panels.description: Prepaid and debit concentration is the classic card-testing signal. Compare against the funding split of your overall refund volume before concluding anything.

panels.title: Disputes in the first 30 days
panels.description: Disputes from customers who had barely started paying. Early disputes skew fraudulent; late ones skew dissatisfied, and the two need opposite responses.

panels.title: Chargeback fees
panels.description: The per-chargeback penalty, which Stripe keeps even on disputes you WIN. It appears nowhere on the dispute object itself.

panels.title: Cancellations
panels.description: Subscriptions that actually ended in this window. A cancellation scheduled for period end is NOT counted here until it completes; that number is 'MRR at risk'.

panels.title: Net MRR movement
panels.description: Signups and upgrades minus downgrades and cancellations, normalised to a month so a yearly plan counts a twelfth per month. Negative means the book shrank.

panels.title: MRR lost to churn
panels.description: The cancellation half of the movement above, on its own.

panels.title: MRR at risk
panels.description: Revenue scheduled to leave but not yet gone: cancellations set for period end, paused collections and failing payments, minus anything that was saved. Deliberately a separate number from the delta, because adding the two would count the same churn twice.

panels.title: Involuntary share

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "subscription_events")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "count" and r.event == "canceled" and (r.churn_type == "voluntary" or r.churn_type == "involuntary"))
  |> keep(columns: ["_value", "churn_type"])
  |> group()
  |> reduce(
      identity: {wanted: 0.0, total: 0.0},
      fn: (r, accumulator) => ({
        wanted: accumulator.wanted + (if r.churn_type == "involuntary" then r._value else 0.0),
        total: accumulator.total + r._value
      })
  )
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _value: if r.total > 0.0 then 100.0 * r.wanted / r.total else 0.0 }))

panels.description: Share of cancellations that were a failed payment rather than a decision. High here is a dunning problem, and no amount of product work will fix it.

panels.title: Recent cancellation comments

targets.query:
from(bucket: "${bucket}")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "subscription_events")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "comment")
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value", "plan_tier", "cancel_feedback"])
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 50)

panels.description: What people wrote when they cancelled. Scrubbed before storage: emails, links, phone numbers and Stripe ids are replaced with placeholders and the text is truncated. It is a redaction, not an anonymisation, so treat it as low-risk free text rather than guaranteed-clean data, and never paste it anywhere public.
